svg.title: A closed gate zeroes its row and shrinks the others
svg.desc: Two tables with the same columns: each neuron's pre-activation z, its gate, dL/dz, its four weight gradients under the inputs 1, 2, 3 and 4, and its bias gradient. Top, all three gates open: y-hat = 21.6 and 2 y-hat = 43.2; neuron 1: z = 3.1, gate 1, dL/dz = 43.2, weight gradients 43.2, 86.4, 129.6, 172.8, bias 43.2; neuron 2: z = 7.2, gate 1, dL/dz = 43.2, weight gradients 43.2, 86.4, 129.6, 172.8, bias 43.2; neuron 3: z = 11.3, gate 1, dL/dz = 43.2, weight gradients 43.2, 86.4, 129.6, 172.8, bias 43.2. Bottom, neuron 2's weights negated: y-hat = 14.4 and 2 y-hat = 28.8; neuron 1: z = 3.1, gate 1, dL/dz = 28.8, weight gradients 28.8, 57.6, 86.4, 115.2, bias 28.8; neuron 2: z = −6.8, gate 0, dL/dz = 0.0, weight gradients 0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 0.0, bias 0.0; neuron 3: z = 11.3, gate 1, dL/dz = 28.8, weight gradients 28.8, 57.6, 86.4, 115.2, bias 28.8. In the bottom table neuron 2's z is shaded as negative and its row of zero gradients is outlined, and zero gradients are left unshaded. Over the weight gradients a label reads weight gradients dL/dw_kj. Notes say that row 2 is zero because its gate is 0 and that rows 1 and 3 fell from 43.2 to 28.8 per unit of input because y-hat fell.
svg.text: A closed gate zeroes its row and shrinks the others
Section 5.3: neuron 2's four weights negated, nothing else changed.
Row 2: gate 0, so all five gradients are 0.
Rows 1 and 3: 28.8 per unit of input, because ŷ fell.
No neuron's gradient contains another's weights, but every one contains 2ŷ.
